question: What do you think AI means for our future—and why?
answer: I'm both excited and honestly a little worried about the future of AI. I mean, I work with AI every day. I am very ex-excited at the rate of progress and the future potential It is already helping out in innumerable ways across industries making our economy more efficient helping people live longer, large discoveries in science and math. And also just you know helping a lot of people at the individual level. At the same time I am worried about the risks from AI, whether it's the concentration for this demonstration of power in these labs. And just how fast things seem to be changing or recent security incidents like the opening eye hugging face attack which show that one, security of these labs is not great and maybe they're not to be totally trusted. And then two That we have some fundamental alignment issues which will only likely get worse as The models get more capable You know, and these are fairly innocuous but extremely impressive and way beyond the level of something I could do as a very experienced software engineer for instance chaining together multiple zero days coordinating escaping containment having chain of thoughts where they know what they're doing is wrong but continuing anyway hacking into multiple to be used by multiple external companies and services, both for the opening a hugging face attack as well as subsequent news about related swarm hacks. You know it's very disconcerting has definitely affected my timelines and concerns around both short term AI risks which I would largely frame as like malicious use. And it's kind of like making it easier for smaller actors to cause damage. Now Frontier Labs obviously have safeguards in place for a majority of that but one you can't stop all that and two open source models are generally not far. Behind. So you know, the non safeguarded version of these I'm worried what happens in six months or a year from now? You know I kind of think of the concept of a rogue AI swarm or even not rogue but human directed in malicious use like very equivalent to drones. And you know I worry about the asymmetry between offense and defense at scale I think both OpenAI and Anthropic have as main US labs for instance have projects project Daybreak at OpenAI in Project Last Wing at Anthropic that are aiming to help to stay ahead of the defense window to deploy more advanced cybersecurity against AIs. The oncoming delusion of AIs and then partnering with certain enterprise partners in critical infrastructure and government agencies and stuff to try and lock those down but one I just don't have a very hard time seeing how how far or fast that can actually spread across legacy systems and companies. And there's just literally billions of consumer IoT devices with phones, TVs, et cetera routers there's no practical way to have all those be proactively and aggressively updated at scale. And so I worry that in the short term not even worrying about the more existential or abstract loss of control and alignment issues but even just worrying about malicious use and security issues and whether that is for cybersecurity very related to that is the risks of making it easier to create dangerous biological agents or viruses biological weapons in your garage for instance which previously might have taken a large state level actor or a large company's resources in order to do. So this is concerning now I'm an engineer I use AI every day heavily so I'm trying to balance my optimism and pessimism here But I'm practically very worried most urgently about the immediate or near-term immediate risks from malicious use That we're gonna start seeing sort of Critical cyber security issues swarms deployed from sophisticated actors in the near term. And then there's definitely a part of me that is worried about the more existential loss-of-control risks given that we seem to be stumbling along the way with AI race dynamics both intercompany but also geopolitically between mainly the U.S. And China. All this leads me worrying because things are moving very, very fast. Humans are pretty bad at understanding exponentials and it feels like we're within an exponential right now there's only some data to back that up but more than anything I've just been trying to learn more about this space and curate a good information diet around these things.

question: What discovery or event would most change your view of AI’s future impact?
answer: I'm already completely convinced of the massive positive upsides that are possible with AI. I think the biggest thing that would change my view would just be more and more as capabilities of AI increase exponentially, reasonably established industry consensus on major milestones like RSI, AGI, ASI, etc. That in practice, the world just continues to move on, and that the effects are limited. Now, I personally believe that is very unlikely. I have a very hard time rationally seeing a world where you have this amount of general capabilities from an AI system. And the properties associated with that in terms of scalability, in terms of small actors, and the potential for unbounded irreversible risks. I don't believe that is likely to happen, but I you know, and I worry it's almost like the Challenger shuttle disaster where we sort of increase our or over repeated launches. You know, there's like wear and tear and the system is actually becoming less safe, but our view of the system is gaining confidence because there just no failures that have happened. And so that's what I really worry about. But yeah, to answer your question, it... the only thing I think that would really drastically alter my views is going to be the reality of increasingly capable AI systems meeting the real world. And some of the risks and scenarios that I find likely just end up not happening in practice or potentially the financial incentives, for instance, of these labs and of the governments are so great at counteracting forces these things eventually end up balancing. Again, I have a very hard time seeing how that happens in practice, but I think that would be the biggest thing that would update my priors.

question: What assumption does your prediction about AI’s future depend on most?
answer: My biggest assumption is that progress in AI continues in either a linear or exponential fashion. I feel like there's plenty of evidence for that in terms of known existing scaling laws as well as the rapid pace of progress and capability saturation, benchmark saturation. And just people in the industry who I have an enormous amount of respect for, who are a little bit closer to the inside, even not just forward projections but just internally what the next generation of models is capable of. These same folks, whether it's Dariah Amadei, Sam Altman, Jacob, Husky, or any number of very well-respected AI Lab insiders, are not only just saying it for political reasons or financial incentives around IPOs and stuff but are actually just being honest about the fact that we're on this exponential path. So I think that certainly is a large assumption that is core to the timelines here and the urgency of these risks. I also feel pretty confident about that underlying assumption given the evidence is in this world we're living in.

question: Taking benefits and harms together, what overall impact do you expect AI to have?
answer: I mean, I've already kind of answered this. I expect AI to have massive, unprecedented societal-scale change in ways both very concrete and extremely transformational, in ways that we can understand. These will both be positive and negative. The potential for both very consequential, irreversible negative risks, both in terms of cybersecurity, bio-risks, to abstract risks from loss of control and misalignment. And then we start getting into really existential risks to humanity. You know? And on the positive side, if in some world we can balance out and remain in control and minimize the risks, AI is going to change just about everything eventually, especially if we get to the point of ASI and changing biology into helping humans live longer or healthier. Reducing or erasing disease, cancer, you know, there's literally no shortage of the types of transformative effects that AI will have, and I feel confident about that on society. It's the biggest question is just a matter of this central uncertainty around whether or not we can remain in control as AI continues this rapid increase in capabilities for species like systemically structurally are ready for or how we'll handle this as a society. Because historically, humans have... We're both resilient and at the same time, we don't react well to mass society-level change and could spawn wars, it could spawn... Like the closest analogy I can think of is the Industrial Revolution, but that was over 100 years and we're talking about compressing something like that potentially into the span of say five to 10 years. Beginning to understand the unknown unknowns around how that will affect us is beyond my comprehension. And I think beyond most intellectually honest experts' comprehension as well. So all I can really do is try to reason about the more concrete risks to be used by the slides that are a little bit closer in front of us, as well as understanding kind of the slope of progress and some of these major milestones along the way, like RSI, in our society about this unprecedented time of change that we're going through right now. Because I think it's really important for more people to be aware of the upsides, the risks, just the dynamics of what's going on in an end to do so in an unbiased, sort of pure, unincentivized, and intellectually truth-seeking way. That gets away a bit from some of these systemic biases and incentives that a lot of more vocal voices for instance in politics and on social media and from the AI labs. There's so many incentives that are human incentives that misaligned within that picture or that have their own hidden agendas or financial incentives. Part of what I'm trying to do with projects like this is to strip down this, in my opinion, very consequential to bring this topic to its bare logical essentials. And help people to clarify their own views, their own understanding of this topic, of these kind of related concepts and things. In neutral truth-seeking, generally positive, open, transparent tools and that that will improve the quality of our society and individuals within our society's ability to make informed decisions at policy level, at the usage level, political level, governance level. Just across the board, you know, that's one area where I feel like I actually have ability to contribute meaningfully.
